Put a jar underneath, open the valve by hand a turn or two, let the water and a little fuel run out until clean diesel comes, then close it finger tight. What comes out is mostly fuel, so keep it away from flames and take it to a recycling center.

diy.t: Read the owner's manual fuel filter section
diy.how: Look up 'water in fuel' or 'fuel filter' in the index. It tells you whether your truck has a hand drain, where it is, and how often the filter is meant to be changed. Some models want the water-in-fuel sensor swapped every time the filter is changed, which is worth knowing before you book the job.

diy.t: Look over the fuel filter housing for leaks
diy.how: Engine off and cool, shine a flashlight on the filter canister. Look for diesel weeping around the cap seal or the drain valve, and for a wet, dirty patch below it. A housing that leaks fuel out also lets air and water in, which is why the light keeps coming back after every drain.

diy.t: Check the fuel cap and filler seal
diy.how: Open the fuel door and look at the rubber ring on the cap. If it is cracked, hard or missing, rain and car wash water can run down into the filler neck. Wipe the neck clean, put the cap back until it clicks, and replace a damaged cap. This is the one cause a driver can fix outright.

dont: Don't set off on a long highway trip with it on. Water in diesel ruins injectors and the high-pressure pump, and those are the costly parts.
Don't keep refuelling at the same pump if the light appeared within a day of filling up there.
Don't pour in an alcohol-based water remover on a modern common-rail diesel unless the owner's manual names that product.
Don't drain the separator near a flame or while smoking. What comes out of it is mostly fuel.

causes2.name: Water collected in the filter or separator
causes2.tell: By far the commonest one, especially on a truck that sits a lot or only does short trips. A little cloudy water drains out, the light goes off, and it creeps back over the following weeks or months.
causes2.fix: A shop drains the separator and normally fits a fresh fuel filter at the same time, since the old one has been sitting in water.

causes2.name: A bad tank of diesel
causes2.tell: The light comes on within a day or two of filling up, often alongside hard starting, rough running or white smoke. What drains out looks milky and there is a lot of it rather than a dribble.
causes2.fix: Drain the separator and replace the filter. In bad cases the tank has to come down to be cleaned and the fuel lines flushed through.

causes2.name: Fuel filter long past its service life
causes2.tell: High mileage since the last filter change, maybe a slight flat spot when you accelerate hard, and the light returning within days of each drain because the filter can no longer hold anything back.
causes2.fix: Replace the diesel fuel filter. Some trucks have two, one on the engine and one under the body, and both get done.

causes2.name: Faulty water-in-fuel sensor
causes2.tell: The light is on but only clean fuel drains out and the engine runs perfectly. The stored code names the water-in-fuel circuit, and a shop can see the sensor reading water that is not there.
causes2.fix: Replace the sensor in the fuel filter housing. On many models it comes as part of the filter kit.

causes2.name: Damaged wiring or connector at the filter housing
causes2.tell: The light comes and goes, often over bumps or in wet weather. A shop finds a chafed wire, a bent pin, or a connector packed with green corrosion at the sensor plug.
causes2.fix: Repair or replace the connector and the short length of damaged wiring behind it.

water-in-fuel-light.shop: The first thing a shop does is open the drain on the water separator and look at what comes out: clean diesel, or cloudy water. Then it reads the stored codes, checks the water-in-fuel sensor and its wiring, and looks the filter housing over for leaks. If a lot of water drains out they will take a fuel sample and check the tank too. Draining and a filter change is usually under an hour. Chasing a sensor or wiring fault is about an hour of diagnosis.

reset.how: This is not a reminder, so there is nothing to reset. On most diesels the light goes out by itself a short time after the water is drained and the engine has run, sometimes after switching the key off and on. If it stays on, either water is still sitting in the filter or the sensor or its wiring has a fault. Clearing the code with a scan tool will not fix either one, and the light will be back.
reset.note: A few makes need the fuel system primed or bled after a drain, and the owner's manual says whether yours is one of them.

faqs.q: How long can I drive with the water in fuel light on?
faqs.a: Check your owner's manual first, because some diesels say to stop the engine and drain the water before restarting. If yours doesn't, keep it to a short, gentle drive to get it drained the same day. Water in diesel damages the injectors and the high-pressure pump, so stop if the engine runs rough or smokes.

faqs.q: Does the light clear itself after I drain the water out?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Once the water is gone and the engine has run for a few minutes the light goes off on its own, sometimes after a key off and on. If it is still on after a proper drain, either water is still in the filter or the sensor itself has failed.

faqs.q: Can I just add a water remover additive instead?
faqs.a: On older diesels some additives help with small amounts of water. On a modern common-rail diesel, add nothing unless the owner's manual names the product, because the wrong one can damage injectors. Draining and a fresh filter is the only fix that actually takes the water out.

faqs.q: Where did the water come from?
faqs.a: Most often from the filling station's own tank, or from moisture condensing inside your tank when it sits part empty through warm days and cold nights. Rain or wash water getting past a cracked fuel cap seal is a less common third way.

faqs.q: Will it fail an inspection or emissions test?
faqs.a: The warning on its own is not usually an inspection item in the United States. But if the trouble has also set an emissions code and lit the check engine light, that can fail you. Rules differ by state, so check your own state's list.

wrench-light.look: A small amber outline of a spanner or wrench, usually low in the middle of the instrument cluster near the speedometer. On Ford and Lincoln it often appears together with a message such as Powertrain Malfunction or Reduced Engine Power. On some other makes the same wrench shape only means routine service is due, so the owner's manual is worth a look.

diy.t: Pull over, shut the engine off, restart
diy.how: Find a safe spot off the road, switch the engine off completely and wait about half a minute. Start it again and see whether the wrench stays on. If it clears and the car feels normal, the fault was a one-off, but it still needs the codes read because the computer saved it.

diy.t: Read the message on the dash screen
diy.how: Look at the small display between the gauges and scroll through it with the buttons on the steering wheel or stalk. Ford and Lincoln usually spell out what the computer is unhappy about, such as reduced power or a transmission fault. Write the exact wording down, because it tells the shop where to start.

diy.t: Check the battery terminals are clean and tight
diy.how: With the engine off and cool, open the hood and look at the two battery posts. If you see white or green crust, or you can wiggle a cable clamp by hand, that is a problem: weak or noisy power upsets the engine and transmission computers. Snug the clamp nuts gently with a small wrench, or have a shop clean them.

diy.t: Look for red or brown drips on the ground
diy.how: Move the car forward a few feet and look at the pavement where it was sitting. Thin red or brown oily spots usually mean transmission fluid, and low transmission fluid is a common reason this light comes on. Do not top it up yourself on most modern cars, as many have no filler tube; just tell the shop what you saw.

dont: Don't tow a trailer or carry a heavy load while the wrench light is on.
Don't keep flooring the gas to force the power back; that can damage the transmission or turbo.
Don't disconnect the battery to make the light go away, because the fault stays and the light returns.
Don't put off a highway trip decision: if power drops out, merging and passing become dangerous.

causes2.name: Electronic throttle body fault
causes2.tell: The engine idles rough or surges, the pedal feels dead or slow, and power is capped. The computer usually stores a throttle or pedal position code such as P2111, P2135 or P0638. A shop can watch the two throttle sensors disagree on a scan tool.
causes2.fix: The throttle body is the air valve the computer opens instead of a cable. It is unbolted from the intake, replaced, and the computer relearns the new one.

causes2.name: Low or worn-out transmission fluid
causes2.tell: Shifts feel hard, slip, or the car seems to hunt between gears, often worse when the transmission is hot. Red or brown drips on the driveway, or a burnt smell from the fluid, point this way. Codes are usually about gear ratio or solenoid performance.
causes2.fix: The shop checks the level the proper way, then drains and refills with the exact fluid that transmission needs. If the fluid is burnt, deeper repairs may follow.

causes2.name: Transmission shift solenoid or speed sensor
causes2.tell: The car gets stuck in one gear, bangs into gear, or refuses to shift above a certain speed, and the wrench comes on while driving. Codes point at a specific solenoid or at input and output shaft speed.
causes2.fix: The solenoid pack or sensor inside the transmission is replaced.

causes2.name: Accelerator pedal position sensor
causes2.tell: Acceleration lags or cuts out, sometimes with no response at all, and the light often appears right after a dead spot in the pedal. The sensor lives on the pedal itself, and the stored code names pedal position.
causes2.fix: The pedal assembly with its sensor is unbolted from under the dash and swapped for a new one, then the computer relearns the idle position.

causes2.name: Turbo boost control fault on EcoBoost engines
causes2.tell: There is a whistle or a sudden flat spot under acceleration, the car feels fine at light throttle, and the wrench appears when you push it. Codes about underboost or overboost, such as P0299, are typical.
causes2.fix: Depending on what is found, the shop replaces a split charge pipe or hose, a boost sensor, or a sticking wastegate actuator on the turbo.

causes2.name: Loose wiring, corroded connector or weak charging
causes2.tell: The light comes and goes, often over bumps or in wet weather, and other warnings may flicker with it. A dim battery light, slow cranking or several unrelated codes at once all suggest voltage or wiring rather than a broken part.
causes2.fix: The shop finds the chafed wire, green connector or failing alternator and repairs that one spot.

wrench-light.shop: The first thing a shop does is plug a scan tool into every computer on the car, not just the engine, because this light is often set by the transmission or all-wheel-drive module. They read the stored codes and the freeze frame data that shows what the car was doing at the time, check battery voltage and the transmission fluid, then look at live throttle and pedal readings. That first look normally takes half an hour to an hour, longer if the fault only shows up on a test drive.

reset.how: This is a fault light, not a service reminder, so there is nothing to reset. Clearing the code with a scan tool or pulling the battery cable turns the wrench off for a while, but it fixes nothing and the light comes back the next time the computer sees the same problem. It can also erase the data a technician needs to find the fault, which makes the repair take longer. Once the broken part is repaired, the light goes out on its own after a few drives.
reset.note: Some of these faults are fixed by a dealer software update rather than a part, and that is still a repair, not a reset.

faqs.q: Can I drive with the wrench light on?
faqs.a: If the car drives and shifts normally, you can usually drive gently home or to a shop. If power is reduced, or the gears slip, bang or jerk, don't drive further than a safe place to stop. Have it towed or checked where it is. Loud noises or a red warning alongside it also mean stop and call for a tow.

faqs.q: Is the wrench light the same as the check engine light?
faqs.a: No. The check engine light covers the engine and its emissions, while the wrench light is a wider powertrain warning that also covers the transmission and, on some models, all-wheel drive. They often come on together, and the wrench can appear on its own with no emissions fault at all.

faqs.q: Will my car pass inspection with the wrench light on?
faqs.a: Rules vary a lot by state, so check your local one. The wrench itself is not the emissions light, but if the check engine light is on too the car will normally fail an emissions test. A car that is stuck in reduced power can also fail a safety inspection because it cannot be driven properly.

faqs.q: Does the wrench light reset itself?
faqs.a: Sometimes it goes off after a few trips if the computer stops seeing the problem, for example after a one-time glitch. That does not mean the fault is gone, because the code stays in memory where a shop can still read it. If it goes out and comes back, treat it as a real fault.

faqs.q: Why does my car feel so slow with this light on?
faqs.a: When the computer no longer trusts a throttle, pedal or transmission reading, it limits power on purpose to protect the engine and transmission. Mechanics call that limp mode. It is the car being careful, not the engine dying, and normal power usually returns once the fault is repaired.

reduced-power-light.look: A turtle drawn from the side, usually amber or yellow, sometimes with words such as POWER DOWN, POWER LIMITED or REDUCED PROPULSION on the screen. It's used on many electric cars and some hybrids and plug-in hybrids. A gas car's reduced engine power warning acts in a similar way but has a different symbol.

diy.t: Check the battery level
diy.how: Look at the battery level on the dash or in the car's app. If it's low, the car is saving what's left. Head for the nearest charger at a gentle speed, and avoid steep hills and fast highway driving on the way.

diy.t: Give the battery a break from heat or cold
diy.how: After a long climb, a fast run or towing on a hot day, the battery and motor can get too hot. Park somewhere shaded, switch the car off and give it 15 to 30 minutes. In freezing weather, parking in a garage or plugging in to charge helps the battery warm up.

diy.t: Write down any other warning
diy.how: Take a photo of any other light or message on the dash. Kia's manual says the power down light on its own is not a failure; it is a fault when a service warning shows with it. A shop will want to know exactly what the screen said.

dont: Don't try to pass or merge into fast traffic while the turtle is on; the car may not speed up when you need it to.
Don't keep driving to see how far you get when the battery is nearly empty; the car can slow to a crawl or stop.
Don't touch orange high-voltage cables or open the battery area.

causes2.name: Battery charge very low
causes2.tell: The battery gauge is near empty and the turtle came on as the range ran down. No other warnings are on.
causes2.fix: Charge the car. The turtle should go out once the battery has enough charge.

causes2.name: Battery or motor too hot
causes2.tell: It came on after a long climb, fast driving, towing or on a very hot day, and went away after the car rested.
causes2.fix: Let the system cool. If it keeps happening in normal driving, a shop checks the battery cooling system, such as the coolant level, pump or fan.

causes2.name: Battery too cold
causes2.tell: It shows on a freezing morning and fades as the car warms up or after charging.
causes2.fix: Park in a garage or plug in so the car can warm the battery. Using the car's preconditioning feature, if it has one, also helps.

causes2.name: Fault in the EV or hybrid system
causes2.tell: A service warning, a check hybrid system message or another light is on with the turtle, or it stays on after charging and cooling.
causes2.fix: A shop that works on EVs and hybrids reads the codes from the battery and motor computers and tests the system.

reduced-power-light.shop: A shop that works on EVs and hybrids reads the codes from the battery and motor control computers, checks the battery's charge and temperature readings, and looks at the battery cooling system. If there is a stored fault, they follow the maker's test steps for it. Many of these checks need dealer-level software.

reset.how: There is nothing to reset. The turtle goes out by itself once the battery has enough charge and is at a normal temperature. If it stays on after that, the car has found a fault that needs to be checked.

faqs.q: Why is there a turtle on my dashboard?
faqs.a: It means the car is cutting back power to protect the high-voltage battery or motor. The battery may be low, too hot or too cold. The car still moves, but slowly, like a turtle.

faqs.q: Will the turtle light go away on its own?
faqs.a: Usually, once you charge the battery or it gets back to a normal temperature. If it stays on after that, or another warning comes on with it, get the car checked.

ready-light.look: The word READY, usually in green, in the gauge cluster or on the screen. Toyota and Lexus hybrids, Hyundai and Kia hybrids and EVs, and many other electrified cars use it. Some electric cars show a green car symbol with arrows instead.
ready-light.flash: On some cars, such as Kia's electric models, a blinking READY means the car can only be driven in a limited emergency mode. Drive only as far as you need to reach a safe place, then have the car checked.

diy.t: Check READY is off before you walk away
diy.how: Every time you park, shift to Park, press the power button and check that READY has gone out. A silent car that is still on can roll if it isn't in Park, and it keeps using the battery.

diy.t: If READY won't come on
diy.how: Press the brake pedal firmly, then press the power button once. If the dash says the key isn't detected, hold the key fob against the power button and try again. If the dash lights up dimly or not at all, the small 12-volt battery may be weak.

dont: Don't get out of the car while READY is on.
Don't assume a quiet car is off; look for the READY light.

causes2.name: Weak 12-volt battery
causes2.tell: READY won't come on, and the dash lights look dim or flicker when you press the power button.
causes2.fix: A shop tests the 12-volt battery and charges or replaces it.

causes2.name: Key fob not detected
causes2.tell: A message says the key isn't detected, or the key fob battery light is on.
causes2.fix: Hold the fob against the power button to start, then replace the fob's coin battery.

causes2.name: Hybrid or EV system fault
causes2.tell: READY blinks or goes out while driving, often with a service warning or check hybrid system message.
causes2.fix: A shop that works on hybrids and EVs reads the system codes.

ready-light.shop: If READY won't come on, a shop tests the 12-volt battery first, because it powers the computers that switch the car on. If READY blinks or drops out while driving, they read the codes from the hybrid or EV system computers and follow the maker's test steps.

faqs.q: Is the car on if it's silent?
faqs.a: It can be. In a hybrid, the gas engine often stays off at low speed, and an electric car never makes engine noise. If READY is lit, the car is on and will move when you press the accelerator in Drive or Reverse.

faqs.q: Why does my hybrid's engine start and stop by itself while READY is on?
faqs.a: That's normal. A hybrid turns its gas engine on and off by itself to charge the battery, warm up or add power.

pre-collision-light.look: A car with a starburst or an exclamation mark in front of it, or two cars close together, usually amber when steady. During a warning, many cars flash a red symbol or a word such as BRAKE! across the screen with fast beeping. Toyota calls it PCS (Pre-Collision System), Honda calls it CMBS, Hyundai and Kia call it Forward Collision-Avoidance Assist, and others call it Forward Collision Warning or Automatic Emergency Braking.
pre-collision-light.flash: A red warning that flashes with fast beeping is the system doing its job: it thinks a crash may be close. Brake and check the road ahead. Kia's manual, for example, says its red forward safety light blinks while the system is working, and no repair is needed for that.

diy.t: Clean the camera area and the front sensor
diy.how: With the car parked, clean the outside of the windshield in front of the rear-view mirror, where the camera looks out. Then wipe the badge or panel in the front grille or lower bumper where the radar sits. Snow, ice, mud, bugs or a sticker there can blind it.
diy.tools: Glass cleaner and a soft cloth

diy.t: Check the settings menu
diy.how: Look in the driver assist or safety settings on the screen. If forward collision warning or automatic braking has been switched off, turn it back on. On many cars it turns itself back on each time you start the car.

diy.t: Let a hot camera cool
diy.how: On a very hot, sunny day the camera behind the windshield can get too hot and switch off for a while. Running the A/C and parking in the shade usually brings it back.

dont: Don't count on automatic braking to stop the car for you; it's a backup, not a replacement for watching the road.
Don't put stickers, dash cams or toll tags in front of the camera behind the mirror.
Don't skip camera calibration after a new windshield.

causes2.name: Blocked camera or radar
causes2.tell: It came on in snow, heavy rain, fog or after a muddy drive, and goes away once the sensor is clean or the weather clears.
causes2.fix: Clean the windshield and the front sensor. No repair is needed.

causes2.name: Camera or radar out of line
causes2.tell: It started after a new windshield, a bumper repair, a small bump or new grille parts.
causes2.fix: A shop with the right equipment recalibrates the camera or radar.

causes2.name: Camera or sensor fault
causes2.tell: It stays on in clear weather with clean sensors, sometimes with a buzzer when it first comes on.
causes2.fix: A shop reads the driver-assist codes and tests or replaces the faulty part.

pre-collision-light.shop: A shop scans the driver-assist computers for codes, checks the camera and radar for damage or anything blocking them, and checks whether they are aimed correctly. If the windshield, bumper or grille was recently replaced, calibrating the camera or radar is often the fix, and that needs special targets and software.

reset.how: There's nothing to reset. A light caused by dirt, weather or heat goes out by itself once the sensor can see again. If it stays on, the fault needs to be checked.

faqs.q: Why did my car beep and flash a warning when nothing was there?
faqs.a: Sometimes the system mistakes a metal plate, a sharp curve or a car turning ahead for something in your path. Treat every warning as a reason to brake and look. If it happens often on clear roads, have the system checked.

faqs.q: Is this the same as the red brake light?
faqs.a: No. The red BRAKE light, or an exclamation mark in a circle, is about the brake system or the parking brake. A flashing collision warning with beeping means brake and look ahead because something may be in your path.

auto-start-stop-light.look: A capital A inside a circle made from a curved arrow. Green or white usually means the system is ready or has stopped the engine. Amber, or the symbol with a line through it or the word OFF, means the system is switched off or has a fault. Kia, for example, shows white when it's ready, green when it has stopped the engine, and yellow for a fault.
auto-start-stop-light.flash: On some cars the green light blinks for a few seconds when the engine restarts by itself. Kia's manual describes a 5-second blink after an automatic restart. That's normal.

diy.t: Try the off button
diy.how: Look for a button with the A-and-arrow symbol, usually near the gear shifter or on the dash. Pressing it switches start-stop off, and a light or OFF message confirms it. On most cars it turns back on the next time you start the car.

diy.t: Think about the battery
diy.how: Start-stop needs a strong 12-volt battery. If the light is amber or the feature has stopped working, and the car also cranks slowly, have the battery tested. Many start-stop cars need a special battery type (often called AGM or EFB), so a replacement must match.
diy.mins: 10 minutes at a shop or parts store

dont: Don't panic if the engine goes quiet at a red light with a green A symbol showing; that's the system working.
Don't fit a cheaper standard battery in a start-stop car; use the type the owner's manual lists.

causes2.name: Battery weak or the wrong type
causes2.tell: Start-stop has stopped working or the light is amber, and the car may crank slowly.
causes2.fix: Test the battery and replace it with the type the maker lists. Some cars need the new battery registered with a scan tool.

causes2.name: Start-stop switched off
causes2.tell: The OFF light came on after the button was pressed.
causes2.fix: Press the button again or restart the car.

causes2.name: Start-stop system fault
causes2.tell: The light is amber and stays on, sometimes after a battery change or a sensor problem.
causes2.fix: A shop reads the codes and checks the battery sensor and related parts.

auto-start-stop-light.shop: A shop tests the 12-volt battery first, checks it's the right type for a start-stop car, and confirms the new battery was registered if the car needs it. Then they read the codes for the start-stop system and check the battery sensor.

faqs.q: My engine shut off at a red light. Is that a stall?
faqs.a: If the green A symbol came on and the engine starts again when you lift off the brake, that's start-stop working. If no symbol showed, warning lights came on, or it won't restart, that's a stall: turn on your hazard lights and see our stalling guide.

faqs.q: Does auto start-stop hurt the engine or starter?
faqs.a: Cars with start-stop are usually built for it, with a tougher starter and battery. The main thing is to replace the battery with the right type when it wears out.

check-fuel-cap-light.look: Some cars show a gas cap symbol or a message such as CHECK FUEL CAP, CHECK GAS CAP or CHECK FUEL FILL INLET. Many others have no separate light and turn on the check engine light instead; Honda's manual, for example, lists a missing or loose fuel cap as one reason for the check engine light.

diy.t: Click the cap shut
diy.how: Turn the engine off. Unscrew the gas cap, look at the rubber ring for cracks or dirt, then screw it back on until you hear it click at least once. If your car has no cap, open the fuel door and check the flap is clean and springs shut.

diy.t: Give it a few days
diy.how: The car only re-tests the fuel vapor system under certain conditions, so the light often stays on for a few days of normal driving after you fix the cap. If it's still on after about a week, have the code read.

dont: Don't smoke or use a lighter near the fuel filler.
Don't buy a cheap cap that doesn't match your car; a poor seal brings the light straight back.

causes2.name: Loose or missing gas cap
causes2.tell: The light came on a day or two after filling up.
causes2.fix: Tighten or replace the cap. The light goes out after some driving.

causes2.name: Worn cap seal
causes2.tell: The cap clicks but the rubber ring is cracked, flat or hard.
causes2.fix: Replace the cap with one that matches your car.

causes2.name: Fuel vapor (EVAP) system leak
causes2.tell: The cap is fine but the light keeps coming back, often with a check engine code such as P0455 or P0456.
causes2.fix: A shop smoke-tests the fuel vapor system to find the leak, often a cracked hose or a stuck valve.

check-fuel-cap-light.shop: A shop reads the code, checks the cap and filler neck, and if those are fine, pushes harmless smoke into the fuel vapor system to see where it escapes. Common finds are a cracked hose, a stuck purge or vent valve, or a damaged filler neck.

reset.how: Once the cap is fixed, the light goes out by itself after the car re-checks the system, which can take a few days of driving. A scan tool can clear it sooner, but if the leak is still there it comes back.

faqs.q: How long after tightening the gas cap does the light go off?
faqs.a: Often a few days of normal driving, because the car only tests the system under certain conditions. If it's still on after about a week, have the code read.

bulb-out-light.look: An amber light bulb with an exclamation mark, or a car outline with one light picked out. Some cars print a message such as CHECK BRAKE LAMP or LOW BEAM OUT, and some, such as many Kias, show it through the master warning triangle with the details on the screen. Cars with LED headlights may have their own headlight warning. If a turn signal arrow on the dash blinks much faster than usual, a bulb on that side is often out.
bulb-out-light.flash: A turn signal that blinks about twice as fast as normal usually means a bulb on that side has burned out. Kia's manual notes it can also be another fault in the turn signal system. If the arrow doesn't blink at all, or stays on without blinking, have the system checked.

diy.t: Do a walk-around light check
diy.how: With the car parked, in Park and the parking brake on, turn on the headlights and hazard lights and walk around the car. Then have a friend watch the back while you press the brake pedal. At night you can also back up close to a garage door or shop window and watch the reflection.
diy.tools: A helper, or a wall or window

diy.t: Check the fuse
diy.how: If both sides of something are out, such as both brake lights, a fuse is more likely than two bulbs at once. The owner's manual shows which fuse to check.
diy.tools: Fuse puller from the fuse box

dont: Don't drive at night with a headlight out if you can avoid it.
Don't fit a brighter or different bulb than the manual lists; it can melt the socket or dazzle other drivers.

causes2.name: Burned-out bulb
causes2.tell: One light is dark, or a turn signal blinks fast on one side only.
causes2.fix: Replace the bulb with the type in the owner's manual. Many are easy to change; some headlights need parts removed first.

causes2.name: Bad socket or connector
causes2.tell: A new bulb works for a while, or flickers when you tap the light.
causes2.fix: Clean or replace the socket and connector.

causes2.name: Blown fuse or wiring fault
causes2.tell: Two or more lights are out at once, such as both brake lights.
causes2.fix: Replace the fuse. If it blows again, have the wiring checked for a short.

causes2.name: Failed LED light unit
causes2.tell: The car has LED lights and a message or headlight warning is on.
causes2.fix: LED lights usually can't be fixed by changing a bulb; the light unit or its control part is replaced.

bulb-out-light.shop: A shop checks which lights work, then tests the bulb, socket, fuse and wiring for the one that doesn't. On cars with LED lights, they read the lighting computer's codes, because the fix is often a whole light unit.

reset.how: Nothing to reset. The warning goes out once the light works again, usually right away or the next time you start the car.

faqs.q: Why is my turn signal blinking fast?
faqs.a: Most often a bulb on that side, front or back, has burned out. Turn on the signal and walk around the car to find which one isn't lit.

faqs.q: Can I get pulled over for a light that's out?
faqs.a: Yes. In most places police can stop you for a headlight, brake light or tail light that isn't working.

ice-warning-light.look: A snowflake, often next to the outside temperature on the dash or screen. Kia's manual says its icy road warning blinks, then stays on with a single chime, when it's about 39°F (4°C) or colder outside. Some cars make the temperature reading flash instead.

diy.t: Check the real temperature
diy.how: Compare the dash reading with a weather app. Right after the car has been parked in the sun or a warm garage, the reading can take a few minutes to catch up.

dont: Don't assume a road that looks wet is just wet: thin clear ice, called black ice, looks the same.
Don't use cruise control on roads that might be icy.

causes2.name: Cold weather
causes2.tell: It's near or below freezing outside.
causes2.fix: Nothing to fix. Drive for the conditions.

causes2.name: Faulty outside temperature sensor
causes2.tell: The light and the temperature reading don't match the weather, for example a freezing reading on a hot day.
causes2.fix: A shop checks the sensor, usually behind the front bumper, and its wiring.

faqs.q: Why does the snowflake come on when it's above freezing?
faqs.a: Roads, especially bridges, can freeze before the air does, so many cars warn a few degrees above 32°F. Kia's manual gives about 39°F (4°C).

od-off-light.look: The letters O/D OFF, usually amber, in the gauge cluster. It's most common on older Toyota and Lexus automatics and some other makes. The button that controls it is usually on the side of the gear shifter.
od-off-light.flash: On some cars, mostly older Toyotas, a flashing O/D OFF light means the transmission computer has found a fault. Drive gently and have the codes read soon.

diy.t: Press the O/D button
diy.how: Press the O/D button on the side of the shifter once. The O/D OFF light should go out. If it comes straight back on, the button may be sticking.

dont: Don't drive on the highway for long with O/D OFF on by mistake; the engine runs faster than it needs to and uses more fuel.

faqs.q: Should I drive with O/D OFF?
faqs.a: Only when your owner's manual suggests it, such as when towing or going down long hills. For normal driving, leave overdrive on.

ev-plug-light.look: A plug with a cable, often next to a car outline, shown while a charging cable is connected. Kia, for example, calls it the charging cable connection indicator. It only appears on electric cars and plug-in hybrids.

diy.t: Release a stuck cable
diy.how: Most cars lock the charging cable in place while charging. Unlock the car with the key fob or the door unlock button, then pull the cable straight out. Many cars also have a manual release inside the trunk or under the hood; the owner's manual shows where.

dont: Don't yank or twist a cable that won't come out; check the owner's manual for the release.
Don't try to drive away while plugged in.

causes2.name: Cable still connected
causes2.tell: The cable is plugged in.
causes2.fix: Unplug it.

causes2.name: Stuck charge port latch or sensor
causes2.tell: The light stays on with nothing plugged in, or the cable won't release.
causes2.fix: A shop that works on EVs checks the port, its lock and its sensor.

faqs.q: Is the plug light the same as the glow plug light?
faqs.a: No. The glow plug light is a coil shape on diesel cars and means the engine is warming up to start. The plug light on an electric car or plug-in hybrid means a charging cable is connected.
